answer: A ledger cannot count heads, but it can trace a pulse of standing as it travels. Let reputation trickle along recorded payment edges: each settled copper transfer leaks a fraction of the sender's standing to the receiver, weakening with every hop. A new wallet starts as a nebula of potential, earning honor only by trading with partners who already hold it. To lift a ring of clones, an attacker must rent genuine counterparties and pay their fees - or loop coins inside the farm, where edges carry no weight.
